questions.question: Explain what barter is and describe two problems of barter.
questions.expected_answer: Barter is the direct exchange of goods or services without money. Problems (any two): needs a double coincidence of wants; no common measure of value; goods hard to divide; perishable goods cannot be stored; bulky goods hard to transport.

questions.question: Put these forms of money in historical order and give one problem each solved: coins, barter, paper money, commodity money.
questions.expected_answer: Barter; commodity money (solved the double coincidence of wants by using one accepted item); coins (durable, divisible, countable, unlike cattle or grain that die or rot); promissory notes and paper money (light and safe to carry compared with heavy coins).

questions.question: List four characteristics of good money and two functions of money. Which institution issues the rand?
questions.expected_answer: Characteristics (any four): generally acceptable, durable, portable, divisible, scarce, uniform. Functions (any two): medium of exchange, measure of value, store of value, standard for deferred payment. The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) issues rand notes and coins.
